temporal_operations.accumulation: combine separately referenced evidence while retaining source, context, contradiction, and uncertainty
temporal_operations.decay: reduce candidate influence or confidence over validity time; never rewrite source truth
temporal_operations.persistence_candidate: propose temporal persistence only when evidence and validity support it; never create permanent state
temporal_operations.recovery: represent movement toward lower activation or restored baseline as a candidate transition
temporal_operations.refresh: new evidence may extend or revise temporal validity with lineage
temporal_operations.repeated_stimulus: repetition may strengthen evidence but cannot alone create permanent emotion or personality
temporal_operations.temporal_validity: every evidence/appraisal/state candidate carries valid-from/valid-until or explicit unknown
temporal_operations.stale_expiration: expired validity produces EXPIRED or historical reference and retains reverse trace
